values.label: Select a solution
values.definition: Choose the task, model family, managed API, or platform approach that fits the required outcome; exclude tuning an already-selected model or configuring its runtime.

values.label: Adapt a foundation model
values.definition: Choose prompting, grounding, supervised or parameter-efficient tuning, or tuning data representation to change a selected foundation model’s task behavior.

values.label: Prepare and move data
values.definition: Choose ingestion, transfer, batch/stream transformation, query/storage layout or dataset preservation; exclude online feature registry semantics and fitted training-serving state.

values.label: Manage shared features
values.definition: Choose feature registration, discoverability, entity/event-time semantics, online views, synchronization or reuse across training and serving.

values.label: Preserve preprocessing state
values.definition: Keep fitted encoders, normalization, tokenizers and transformations consistent across training and inference; merely sharing code is not enough.

values.label: Validate quality
values.definition: Choose held-out populations, splits, comparison metrics, fairness slices or offline evaluation that make a quality claim or release gate meaningful; not ongoing telemetry setup.

values.label: Optimize training
values.definition: Choose a training objective/loss, search method, search space, regularization or trial strategy; exclude hardware sizing and foundation-model adaptation method.

values.label: Provision workload compute
values.definition: Choose hardware, parallelism, job packaging, checkpointing or resource shape for execution; exclude serving replica scaling and interactive notebook setup.

values.label: Package inference
values.definition: Choose batch versus online execution, serving containers, request/response handlers, model loading or runtime routes; exclude traffic rollout and replica policy.

values.label: Scale serving capacity
values.definition: Choose serving scaling signal, replicas, warm capacity, concurrency or capacity reservation to match demand.

values.label: Release safely
values.definition: Choose rollout, rollback, traffic allocation or stable experiment cohorts across versions; not merely recording a version or gating a build.

values.label: Orchestrate a workflow
values.definition: Choose a workflow runner, component graph, dependency passing, reusable template or execution cache for a multi-step process.

values.label: Trigger lifecycle automation
values.definition: Choose when to run retraining/builds/jobs or how approvals and event triggers start lifecycle actions; exclude component graph design and traffic rollout.

values.label: Track versions and provenance
values.definition: Choose model version grouping, mutable aliases, experiment records or artifact/execution lineage to reproduce, compare or trace results.

values.label: Monitor behavior
values.definition: Choose operational telemetry, drift/skew/output baselines, recurring quality/fairness checks, sampling or alerting for a running system; not one-time candidate validation.

values.label: Explain predictions
values.definition: Choose local/global feature attribution, explanation baseline or interpretation method matching the requested explanatory scope.

values.label: Protect information
values.definition: Choose de-identification, encryption, prompt/output screening or security-threat controls at the right data-flow boundary; access identities and private network setup belong to manage_access.

values.label: Manage access and boundaries
values.definition: Choose identity, permission scope, hierarchy/policy placement or private network connectivity. Includes resource organization only when it determines control or ownership.

values.label: Configure a development environment
values.definition: Choose interactive workspace, notebook sharing, language/dependency isolation or development-tool integration; exclude production training jobs.

values.label: Cost or work budget
values.definition: Money, token/compute spend, repeated processing or bounded trials constrain the choice.

values.label: Operational effort
values.definition: Minimize owned code, servers, maintenance, manual coordination or required specialist skills. Do not infer this solely from the word managed.

values.label: Latency or deadline
values.definition: An end-to-end response-time, cold-start or completion-time requirement discriminates alternatives.

values.label: Capacity or scale
values.definition: Demand, data volume, memory, throughput or concurrency changes feasibility; volume alone is not enough unless it affects the decision.

values.label: Reliability or availability
values.definition: Keep operations available, recover from interruption, avoid duplicate/lost work or support safe fallback.

values.label: Security, privacy or residency
values.definition: Protect confidentiality, least privilege, regulated data, location or an explicit trust boundary.

values.label: Compatibility or retained control
values.definition: Preserve an existing framework, language, protocol, dependency, interface or required customization; existing alone is not sufficient.

values.label: Freshness or event timing
values.definition: Use sufficiently current data, event-time meaning, timely updates or correct label-maturity windows.

values.label: Data or state consistency
values.definition: Preserve schemas, entity joins, fitted representations or equivalent behavior across runs and environments.

values.label: Measurement validity
values.definition: Use appropriate metric, reference population, holdout, causal cohort or subgroup evidence for the actual business question.

values.label: Traceability or reproducibility
values.definition: Recover exact cohorts, versions, artifacts or provenance to reproduce or audit a past result.

values.label: Wrong capability or abstraction
values.definition: Alternative cannot perform the required task or chooses the wrong task/model/service interface.

values.label: Wrong metric, scope or reference
values.definition: Measures a proxy or wrong population/baseline instead of the requested quality, fairness or explanation.

values.label: State or representation mismatch
values.definition: Breaks fitted transformations, schemas, versions, entity/time alignment or reproducible inputs.

values.label: Wrong boundary or timing
values.definition: Applies protection/control after exposure, at the wrong layer, or uses stale/immature data at the wrong moment.

values.label: Avoidable operational work
values.definition: Adds custom infrastructure, manual coordination or migration without a scenario benefit.

values.label: Wasted resources
values.definition: Consumes unnecessary compute, storage, tokens, trials or idle capacity while a feasible lower-work choice exists.

values.label: Insufficient capacity or scaling signal
values.definition: Uses a poor scaling metric, replica/memory allocation, warm-up strategy or parallelism for demand.

values.label: Excessive or wrong access scope
values.definition: Uses incorrect identity, broad grant, group/hierarchy scope or location policy.

values.label: Unsafe lifecycle or delivery
values.definition: Loses work, disrupts availability, mixes experiment cohorts, bypasses approval or lacks safe rollout/recovery.

values.label: Unsupported assumption or configuration
values.definition: Relies on unsupported compatibility/settings or assumes guarantees not supplied by the scenario; use only when the rationale explicitly supports this, never as a miscellaneous label.
